question: What will be the seasonally adjusted month-on-month percentage change in New Zealand's total electronic card transaction values for October 2026 (Stats NZ, released 12 November 2026)?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: SA total ECT monthly changes centre near +0.2% (nominal growth ~3%/yr) with SD ~0.9pp; 2026 prints range -1.6 to +2.2. August and September 2026 were both -0.5%, leaving room for mean reversion. Fuel prices rose further into October (record 91 above $3.50 early Oct, spikes mid-month, ~$3.56 at month end), adding perhaps +0.2-0.4pp via the ~5-6% fuel weight. Offsetting: discretionary weakness (hospitality, apparel down two months), October consumer confidence dipped to 96.2, and buying-intentions worsened. No October NZ card tracker found. Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers. Median +0.2, wide tails.
calls.dossier:
- Stats NZ ECT Sep 2026 (released 16 Oct 2026): SA total all industries -0.5% (-$51m); retail -0.4%; core retail -0.7%; fuel +2.9%; hospitality -2.3%. (Xinhua 16 Oct 2026; Westpac First Impressions Oct 2026)
- Stats NZ ECT Aug 2026: SA total -0.5% (-$48m); retail -0.9%; core -1.1%; actual total $9.4bn. (Stats NZ / search summary)
- Earlier 2026 SA total changes: Jan -0.7, Apr -1.6, May +2.2, Jul +1.0, Aug -0.5, Sep -0.5 (question background plus Stats NZ Aug release).
- Westpac (Oct 2026): Sep retail -0.4% versus a +0.8% forecast; hospitality and apparel down two months running; groceries up modestly; expects near-term spending to stay subdued as fuel costs stay high and wage growth weak.
- Fuel: NZ petrol +6.4% in Sep 2026; 91 average hit a record above $3.50 on about 5 Oct 2026 (1News); some pumps above $4 by 16 Oct (1News); 91 average about $3.556/L on 31 Oct (dailyfuels). The October average fuel price is likely above September's. Fuel is about 5-6% of total ECT value.
- ANZ-Roy Morgan NZ consumer confidence Oct 2026: 96.2, down 1.4; 'bad time to buy a major item' net -17, down 10 points (Roy Morgan).
- RBNZ credit card spending Sep: +6.9% y/y, which includes foreign cards (newsquawk).
- Calendar: Oct 2026 has 5 Saturdays and Labour Day (26 Oct); seasonal adjustment should account for these but adds noise. An NZ election is around early Nov 2026.
- Status quo / base rate: over all monthly SA total changes, the median is about +0.2% and SD about 0.9pp. After two consecutive declines there is no strong documented conditional pattern (searched, absent).
- Resolves off the Stats NZ 'Electronic card transactions: October 2026' release (12 Nov 2026), using the total all-industries SA % change, not the retail or core retail figures.
- Event window: October 2026 spending, reported 12 Nov 2026; as of 2 Nov the month is complete but no October data has been published.
- Searched but not found: an NZ bank (Westpac/BNZ/ANZ/Worldline) card tracker for Oct 2026 (the Westpac-DataX tracker found is Australian); any prediction market (none found).
calls.reference_class: Monthly seasonally adjusted % changes in Stats NZ total (all-industries) ECT value, 2024-2026

calls.reasoning: Reference class: SA monthly % changes in the Stats NZ ECT total (all industries) series. These are noisy, near-zero-mean moves with SD ~1pp; 2026 prints were -0.7, -1.6, +2.2, +1.0, -0.5 (Aug), -0.5 (Sep). October fuel prices hit record highs (91 at ~$3.52/L on 7 Oct after +15.9% in 28 days; ~$3.56 on 31 Oct), so October's average pump price was ~8-10% above September's. Fuel is ~5-6% of total card spend, which implies roughly +0.3-0.5pp, partly offset by lower volumes. Mean reversion after two -0.5% months adds a little upside. Against that: consumer confidence fell to 96.2, Paymark retail spending was negative y/y in Aug and Sep, and a fuel squeeze crowds out discretionary spending. Median ~+0.3 with wide tails. No market found: Polymarket and Kalshi are barred in NZ, and none was found on Manifold.
calls.dossier:
- Stats NZ ECT Sep 2026 (released 16 Oct 2026): SA total all industries -$51m (-0.5%); retail -0.4% (-$30m); core retail -0.7%; fuel +2.9% (+$15m); hospitality -2.3%; apparel -2.0%; durables -0.5%; consumables +0.3%; motor vehicles +0.6%. Actual total ~$9.2b. (question text; scoop.co.nz; fx.co)
- Stats NZ ECT Aug 2026 (released 15 Sep): SA total -$48m (-0.5%); retail -0.9% (-$63m); all retail categories fell except fuel (+1.3%). (stats.govt.nz Aug release via search)
- Reported 2026 SA total m/m changes: Jan -0.7, Apr -1.6, May +2.2, Jul +1.0, Aug -0.5, Sep -0.5 (Feb, Mar, Jun not found). Sample SD ~1.2pp; long-run history suggests ~0.8-1.0pp.
- Fuel prices: RNZ 7 Oct 2026, 91 at $3.52/L (+15.9% over 28 days), diesel $3.23 (+18%); 1News 5 Oct record high; 1News 16 Oct some stations above $4; 31 Oct national average 91 $3.556, diesel $3.206 (fuelwatch via search); globalpetrolprices 26 Oct NZD 3.73 (95). October average pump price appears ~8-10% above September's average. Fuel is ~5-6% of total ECT value.
- RNZ 7 Oct: petrol demand down ~6% in Q2-Q3 2026, smaller fill-ups; ANZ fuel spending +11.2% y/y in September.
- ANZ-Roy Morgan consumer confidence Oct 2026: 96.2, down 2 points, eighth month below 100 (fx.co).
- Paymark core retail: Aug -1.8% y/y, Sep -1.3% y/y, attributed to petrol, interest rates and bad weather (newswire.co.nz, Oct 2026). ANZ card spending SA +0.5% in Sep (contrasts with the Stats NZ -0.5%).
- Calendar: October 2026 has five Saturdays and Labour Day on 26 Oct; seasonal adjustment should handle these, but residual calendar noise is possible.
- Status quo / persistence: monthly SA changes show weak autocorrelation, with a tendency to partially reverse after large moves.
- Resolves off the Stats NZ 'Electronic card transactions: October 2026' release of 12 Nov 2026 (first-published SA total all-industries % in the headline sentence), not ANZ, Paymark or RBNZ data.
- Event window: the October 2026 month vs September 2026; the release on 12 Nov 2026 resolves it. As of 2 Nov the month is 100% elapsed and the number is unpublished.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: 2026 monthly SA total ECT changes, centred near zero with SD about 1pp. Aug and Sep were both -0.5%, so some mean reversion is plausible. Petrol hit record highs in early October (91 octane >$3.50/L), which mechanically lifts nominal fuel spending by roughly 0.2-0.4pp of the total. Against that: squeezed households, falling retail and hospitality, and a weak October payment-volume remark in Worldline's Q3 deck (not NZ data, since Worldline sold its NZ unit in May 2026). Market check: no Kalshi contract (Kalshi is restricted for NZ users), none on Polymarket or Manifold per the harness search, no bookmaker found. Median +0.2, with dispersion kept at the reference-class width.

calls.reference_class: Stats NZ seasonally adjusted total ECT month-on-month changes, 2025-2026

calls.reasoning: Base rate: SA total ECT m/m changes centre near +0.1-0.2% (low nominal growth) with SD ~0.9pp. October fuel prices averaged roughly 8% above September (record 91 >$3.50 from early Oct, ~$3.56 at month end); with fuel ~5-6% of total spend and visible volume compression (Sep fuel card spend +2.9% vs pump price +6.4%), that adds ~+0.2-0.3pp. Mild mean reversion after two -0.5% months adds a little. Offsets: discretionary weakness (hospitality/apparel down two months), October consumer confidence 96.2 and worse buying intentions. Median +0.2, reference-class width. No market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmakers.
calls.reconciliation: Runs agreed on all checkable facts (Sep -0.5%, Aug -0.5%, 2026 prints, record October fuel prices, Oct confidence 96.2, no market). Factual dispute was only the size of the Oct-vs-Sep average fuel price rise (5-8% vs 8-10%). RNZ's +15.9% over 28 days to 7 Oct plus the ~$3.56 month-end level imply ~8%. That cannot be pinned further without web access, and it matters little: Sep data show volumes absorbing about half the price rise, so the net fuel contribution is ~+0.2-0.3pp under either figure. The rest is judgment (discretionary drag vs mean reversion), where I take the slightly more cautious +0.2 median because the Sep fuel pass-through was weak. Small escape masses reflect ~1% two-sided normal tails plus fatter real tails (May 2026 printed +2.2). Carried the runs' reference class and dispersion forward because I agree with them.

disagreements.verdict: Dossier points (+15.9% over 28 days to 7 Oct, ~$3.56 at month end) imply ~8%; not further checkable offline; low impact after the volume offset
